close_reason: No action needed. This bead documents that the current Clearable<T> + Option<Clearable<T>> + some_clearable factoring is correct for JMAP /set tri-state patch semantics (absent / null / set). The bead's primary value is as a tripwire for future contributors who might propose Option<Option<T>>, plain T with default+deserialize_with, or adding #[non_exhaustive] to Clearable (which would break exhaustive matching). The factoring is already explicitly documented in clearable.rs:32. Keeping the bead's reasoning preserved in the close comment.
description:
Why this is correct: JMAP /set update operations have three patch-field states per nullable field: absent (leave unchanged), present-as-null (clear), present-with-value (set). A naïve Option<Option<T>> deserialize collapses absent and null to the same None. The naïve fix (custom Deserialize on each field) is verbose and fails to compose.

The current approach (crate-jmap-chat-types/src/clearable.rs):
- Clearable<T> as a two-variant enum (Clear / Set(T)) — deliberately NOT #[non_exhaustive] because exhaustive match-ability is the whole point.
- Field shape: #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none, deserialize_with = some_clearable)] pub field: Option<Clearable<T>>.
- some_clearable wraps the inner Deserialize in Some so absent (caught by default) stays None while present (including null) goes through Clearable's own deserialize.
- Serialize: Clearable::Clear → serialize_none → null; Clearable::Set(v) → v. The wrapping Option handles 'skip when None'.

What a future contributor might incorrectly suggest changing:
- 'Use #[serde(default, deserialize_with)] on a plain T?' — loses the null-vs-absent distinction.
- 'Use Option<Option<T>>?' — loses the null-vs-absent distinction in the deserialize layer; serde collapses them.
- 'Add #[non_exhaustive] to Clearable for consistency with the rest of the crate?' — breaks exhaustive matching, which is the entire point of this helper. Already correctly documented in clearable.rs:32 with 'Not #[non_exhaustive] — callers must be able to match exhaustively on Clear / Set.'
- 'Inline the deserialize_with closure instead of factoring out some_clearable?' — sprays the same trick across 5+ patch struct fields, all of which need #[allow(dead_code)] for the rustc tracking issue.

The three-piece factoring is the minimum needed to make patch fields ergonomic and the wire semantics exact. Preserve.
title: Clearable<T> + Option<Clearable<T>> + some_clearable helper: the right shape for tri-state patch semantics
